description: Self-test for the diagnostic `message` opt-in (issue #1025). A fixture opts in with the explicit top-level `"compareMessages": true`; without it, an expected diagnostic carrying a `message` is a fixture ERROR rather than silently-ignored data, which is what makes "present-but-ignored" structurally impossible instead of merely cleaned up once. This fixture proves the opt-in has teeth. Every other field -- `code`, `source_span` (document, start and end), `params`, `stage`, `severity` -- is identical to what `check()` actually produces for `define forward :n`, so the ONLY thing that can make the harness report a mismatch is the message, and `expect: "mismatch"` turns that detection into a pass. That claim is not asserted but controlled: deleting just the `message` line makes the streams MATCH and this self-test then FAILS with `expected mismatch but streams matched` -- run it. The wrong sentence used here is not invented: it is issues #751 and #871 verbatim, which shipped twice and leaked the word *primitive* at a learner -- `spec/error-model.md:125` makes *keyword*, *primitive* and *alias* a MUST NOT in this message, and a MUST NOT about message text is unenforceable by a harness that never reads message text. Using the real regression wording rather than a neutral sentinel has one known consequence, accepted deliberately (`@testing` F4): a genuine regression to that sentence makes THIS fixture flip to `expected mismatch but streams matched` too, so it reads as a harness fault beside the real producer failures. The documentary value of quoting the exact sentence the corpus must reject was judged worth it, and the accompanying `ol-reserved-word` fixtures name the producer unambiguously. Two neighbouring arms live in scripts/conformance.test.mjs instead, because no fixture can express either: a diagnostic whose prose differs while the fixture has NOT opted in (it would have to record the prose it is not asserting), and the opt-in flag itself being rejected when nothing carries a message.

diagnostics.message: forward is already a reserved primitive, so it can't be redefined here.
